title: Inflight request queue fairness causing tenant burst-starvation
creator: Miguel Santos
description: Summary: Multiple customers (notably MediTrust) escalated after observing sustained 503s and high tail latencies during burst windows despite nominal reserved-pool headroom. Investigation points to a recent change (scheduler v2) that altered inflight-request fairness: inflight slots were rebalanced by age across tenants, which unintentionally created long-lived tail queues for small/low-priority tenants and prevented the autoscaler from clearing burst reservations. Customer impact: intermittent request failures, degraded p95/p99 generation latencies, and perceived capacity shortfalls for affected tenants. Scope: Hosted and Dedicated pools with mixed-tenant workloads; Private deployments using the same scheduler binary may be affected if they pulled the v2 runtime. Goal: triage customer impact, implement a targeted hotfix to restore predictable burst behavior, and harden the scheduler to prevent recurrence.
steps_reproduced: 1) Send synthetic mixed-tenant load: 70% large-tenant steady stream, 30% small-tenant short bursts (50-200 reqs/s) to a reserved pool.
2) Observe inflight request queue lengths: small tenants show rising enqueued_count while large tenants hold many inflight slots for long-running responses.
3) Trigger a burst for small tenant and watch reserved-pool utilization: autoscaler does not reclaim or allocate burst buffer; small tenant requests time out or get 429/503.
4) Reproduce in staging with scheduler v1 (control) and v2 (regression) to confirm behavioral difference.
5) Capture logs and traces: scheduler decisions, slot assignment timestamps, and kv-cache eviction events correlate with enqueued durations > 12s for affected tenants.
Environment: cluster-prod-us-west-1, runtime-2.3-scheduler-v2, reserved-pool tier=medium, mixed-tenant networking profile.
investigation_notes: 2026-03-10 09:12 - Pager: MediTrust reported 40% increase in 503s during morning burst window; support triaged to infra; elevated to ENG.
2026-03-10 11:03 - Initial telemetry: p95 token latency up 3.2x for 3 tenants; overall reserved-pool headroom reported as 'available' per collector but tenant-level enqueued time high.

2026-03-11 14:45 - Diff between scheduler v1 and v2: v2 introduced 'age-based fairness' which transfers inflight slot ownership by request age rather than tenant weight. Edge case: long-running streaming responses keep slots occupied and count towards fairness, starving bursty short requests on other tenants.

2026-03-12 08:58 - Root cause hypothesis: age-based fairness attempted to reduce starvation for long-waiting requests, but because it didn't consider per-tenant reserved-burst quotas and the autoscaler's perception of 'occupied slots' excludes enqueued slots, the system misclassifies availability and avoids allocating burst capacity, leading to effective capacity shortfall.
2026-03-12 10:20 - Confirmed with local sim: when average response time for top tenant > 2.5s and small-tenant burst < 1s, starvation reproducible with v2 but not v1.

2026-03-13 16:05 - Customer impact assessment: 7 customers saw degraded SLAs; 2 enterprise customers (including MediTrust) opened urgent escalations. Estimated incidents hours: ~18 across affected clusters.
mitigation_and_hotfix: Immediate mitigation (done 2026-03-12 13:00): rolled back scheduler-v2 for affected Dedicated clusters (prod-us-west-1, prod-eu-central-1) to scheduler-v1 to stop new occurrences and reduce customer impact.

Short-term hotfix (in review): patch scheduler-v2 to recognize 'reserved-burst' marker on tenants and avoid age-based rebalancing that withdraws burst-qualified inflight slots. Patch branch: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4127.

Workaround for customers: recommended pinning to dedicated-reserved-pool-config with 'burst_preference: reserved' in tenant config (docs link below) and enabling temporary tenant-priority override for MediTrust until patch deployed.
Monitoring added: inflight_slot_wait_time_p50/p95 metrics + alert when small-tenant enqueued_count > 5% of pool and autoscaler headroom > 15% (to capture mismatch).
rollout_plan: 1) Merge hotfix PR after 1 LGT (expected by 2026-03-15 AM).

2) Canary deploy patched scheduler-v2 to staging and one non-critical production pool (prod-us-east-2) for 4 hours with synthetic canary load. Success criteria: no enqueued starvation for small-tenant bursts, stable autoscaler decisions.

3) If canary passes, staged rollout to Dedicated clusters in priority order: eu-central-1, us-west-1, us-east-2, us-west-2 across 48 hours with automated rollback on anomaly detection (metric thresholds defined).
4) Communicate to affected customers ahead of rollout window; coordinate with accounts to disable tenant-priority overrides once stable.
5) Post-deploy: schedule 72-hour monitoring window and 1-week follow-up audit to ensure recurrence rate < 0.1% of previous baseline.
testing_plan: Unit tests: add regression test for per-tenant reserved-burst honor when doing fairness rebalancing.
Integration tests: end-to-end sim with mixed-tenant synthetic workload reproducing previous starvation pattern, assert request success rate for bursts > 99%.
Load test: ramp mixed traffic to 200% of baseline; validate autoscaler responds and reserved-burst tenants get expected headroom.
Chaos test: introduce long-running streaming responses and validate scheduler doesn't reassign burst slots away from reserved tenants.
Observability: add dashboard slice for 'inflight_slot_age_by_tenant' and 'reserved_burst_starvation_incidents'.
follow_ups: Postmortem due: 2026-03-22 owner: Aisha Patel. Deliverable: timeline, decision matrix for fairness algorithm changes, and recommended guardrails for future scheduler heuristics.
Engineering follow-up: implement per-tenant inflight cap + exponential backoff for fairness transfers (estimate 13pt, follow-up ticket ENG-1010110).
Product follow-up: document changes and notify Dedicated customers about scheduler behavior differences in runtime-2.x release notes.
SRE: add runbook section for 'burst-starvation' incidents with checklist to verify scheduler version and temporarily revert if needed.
Customer success: schedule 1:1 with MediTrust on 2026-03-19 to review incident, confirm runbook, and provide credits as appropriate.
